title: Gochujang Fried Noodles
description: gochujang noodles with eggs, whichever vegetables we have, and Spam, beef or cooked chicken.
imageAlt: Reference photograph of fried noodles with prawns in a glass serving bowl.
imageCaption: Reference photograph · seafood fried-noodle variation · displayed crop
personalNote: Use whichever vegetables we have. Same wok method as our gochujang fried rice, but with egg noodles tonight.
advancePrep: Chop the garlic and ginger, or check the freezer for ginger-garlic blocks. If we use pak choi, separate the greens and cut the stalks into matchsticks.
importantNotes: This makes four portions across two dinners for both of us. Pick one protein using the tabs, and use one of the vegetable options in the ingredient note. Get everything ready before the wok goes on. Fresh pak choi or beansprouts need about 2 minutes; frozen vegetables need 5 minutes. The times are estimates. Boil the egg noodles using the packet instructions before they go into the wok.
choiceHeading: Spam, beef or cooked chicken tonight?
choiceIntro: Pick the protein. I’ve kept the rest of the wok method the same.

ingredients.name: Egg noodles
ingredients.note: Boil separately using the packet instructions.

ingredients.name: Garlic
ingredients.note: Peel and chop. Or replace this and the ginger with 2 frozen ginger-garlic blocks for the batch.

ingredients.name: Ginger
ingredients.note: Peel and chop; omit if using the ginger-garlic blocks.

ingredients.name: Pak choi
ingredients.note: Or choose 200 g frozen peas, 200 g mixed frozen vegetables, or 1 pack beansprouts. Use whichever ONE option we have. For pak choi, separate leaves and cut the stalks into matchsticks.

ingredients.name: Water for preparing the noodles
ingredients.note: For boiling; cold running water too if we are making fresh rice.

ingredients.name: Sesame oil
ingredients.note: For a drizzle at the table.

steps.title: Add the garlic and ginger
steps.description: Add the chopped garlic and ginger, or the ginger-garlic blocks, and fry for another 2 minutes. Squish them around and keep an eye on the garlic so it doesn’t go black.

steps.title: Scramble the eggs
steps.description: Crack in the eggs and scramble them around for 3 minutes, until they’re set.

steps.title: Add whichever vegetables we chose
steps.description: Add the vegetables. If we’re using fresh pak choi or beansprouts, cook for 2 minutes. If we chose frozen peas or mixed frozen vegetables, cook for 5 minutes instead. Squish everything around so it heats evenly.
steps.tip: This 2-minute timer is for fresh vegetables. Frozen vegetables need 5 minutes; cook longer if their packet requires it.

steps.title: Mix in the gochujang and soy
steps.description: Add the gochujang and light soy sauce, and squish them around with everything for 1 minute.

steps.title: Fry the noodles until hot
steps.description: Now add the well-drained cooked egg noodles and fry for 5–10 minutes, tossing and squishing it around, until it’s nice and hot all the way through. Keep the noodles moving so the sauce gets mixed through.
steps.tip: The 5-minute timer is the first check. Keep going for up to 10 minutes if it needs it.

steps.title: Serve dinner
steps.description: Serve straight away with lime wedges and sesame oil. For the Spam or beef batch, put the second dinner into small containers to cool promptly. For cooked chicken, make the second dinner fresh using the portion of chicken we kept chilled and unheated.

recipeOptions.label: Spam
recipeOptions.description: Spam tonight? Dice it nice and fine, then give it 3 minutes in the hot wok.

ingredients.name: Spam
ingredients.note: Dice finely—smaller than we do for the pork stew.

beforeSteps.title: Get everything ready for the spam version
beforeSteps.description: Dice the Spam finely, smaller than we do for the pork stew. Chop the garlic and ginger, or use the freezer blocks. Choose whichever one vegetable option we have. If it’s pak choi, separate the leaves and cut the stalks into matchsticks. Have the eggs and sauces ready too.

beforeSteps.title: Boil the egg noodles
beforeSteps.description: Boil the egg noodles separately using the packet’s instructions, then drain them. We’re using noodles instead of the rice, and the rest of the wok method stays the same.

beforeSteps.title: Fry the Spam
beforeSteps.description: Get the wok hot on high heat and add the finely diced Spam. Fry it for 3 minutes, moving it around so it starts to brown.

recipeOptions.label: Thin beef steaks
recipeOptions.description: Beef tonight? Use thin slices and start with a 7-minute searing check.

ingredients.name: Thin beef steaks
ingredients.note: Slice thinly. Use in place of the Spam.

beforeSteps.title: Get everything ready for the beef version
beforeSteps.description: Slice the beef steaks thinly. Chop the garlic and ginger, or use the freezer blocks. Choose whichever one vegetable option we have. If it’s pak choi, separate the leaves and cut the stalks into matchsticks. Have the eggs and sauces ready too.

beforeSteps.title: Boil the egg noodles
beforeSteps.description: Boil the egg noodles separately using the packet’s instructions, then drain them. We’re using noodles instead of the rice, and the rest of the wok method stays the same.

beforeSteps.title: Sear the thin beef steaks
beforeSteps.description: Get the wok hot on high heat and add the thinly sliced beef. Start with 7 minutes, turning and checking it for a good brown sear. Keep cooking if it needs longer, until it’s cooked through; don’t let it burn.
beforeSteps.tip: The 7-minute timer is the first check. Keep cooking until you’re happy the beef is cooked through.
beforeSteps.doneness: A good brown sear and beef cooked through.

recipeOptions.label: Cooked chicken
recipeOptions.description: Cooked chicken tonight? Follow the Spam’s 3-minute timing. I’ve set the portion control to two for tonight; keep tomorrow’s chicken chilled and unheated, and make that dinner fresh so we don’t reheat it twice.

beforeSteps.title: Get everything ready for the chicken version
beforeSteps.description: Have the already cooked chicken ready in small pieces. Chop the garlic and ginger, or use the freezer blocks. Choose whichever one vegetable option we have. If it’s pak choi, separate the leaves and cut the stalks into matchsticks. Have the eggs and sauces ready too.

beforeSteps.title: Boil the egg noodles
beforeSteps.description: Boil the egg noodles separately using the packet’s instructions, then drain them. We’re using noodles instead of the rice, and the rest of the wok method stays the same.

beforeSteps.title: Fry the cooked chicken
beforeSteps.description: Get the wok hot on high heat and add the already cooked chicken. Fry it for 3 minutes, following the Spam timing, then carry on with the garlic and eggs.
beforeSteps.warning: Use properly chilled cooked chicken that has not already been reheated.

substitutions.title: Frozen ginger-garlic blocks
substitutions.text: Use 2 frozen blocks instead of the head of garlic and 50 g ginger for this batch.

substitutions.title: Use whichever vegetables we have
substitutions.text: Choose 2 packs pak choi, 200 g frozen peas, 200 g mixed frozen vegetables, or 1 pack beansprouts. Fresh vegetables get 2 minutes in the wok; frozen ones get 5 minutes.

substitutions.title: Protein amounts
substitutions.text: The usual version uses one can of Spam. We can use thin beef steaks or the cooked chicken instead; pick one using the tabs above.

troubleshooting.title: Keeping the noodles moving
troubleshooting.text: Drain the boiled noodles and keep tossing them through the sauce while they fry.

troubleshooting.title: Frozen veg needs longer
troubleshooting.text: Give frozen vegetables 5 minutes, rather than the fresh vegetables’ 2 minutes. Follow their packet if it needs longer.

storage: For Spam or beef, divide the second dinner into small containers to cool quickly, then refrigerate within 1–2 hours and eat within 48 hours. For the cooked-chicken version, keep the unheated chicken for night two properly chilled and within its safe storage time, then make that dinner fresh.
reheating: Reheat the saved Spam or beef dinner once until steaming hot throughout, stirring or turning it to avoid cold pockets.  With cooked chicken, fry a fresh dinner portion rather than reheating chicken that we have already heated once.
foodSafety: The beef must be cooked through. Use properly chilled cooked chicken that has not already been reheated, and heat tonight’s meal until steaming hot throughout. Keep the remaining cooked chicken unheated for the second dinner, and reheat it only once when we cook that portion.
servingSuggestion: Serve straight away with lime wedges and sesame oil. This batch gives us a second dinner too.
